bull.b: Rapid revenue growth alongside an approximately 90% gross margin indicates improving product economics and growing commercial traction. If this pattern persists, high gross profit conversion could support future reinvestment and operating leverage as prescription volume expands.

Repeat purchasing and favorable mature-cohort refill patterns provide evidence that VIZZ can generate ongoing treatment demand rather than only initial prescriptions. Durable persistence would improve customer lifetime value, strengthen commercial economics, and support more predictable revenue growth.

A growing international partner network and multiple regulatory submissions broaden the potential addressable market without relying solely on U.S. execution. Successful approvals and launches could create additional product, licensing, and milestone revenue streams over the next several quarters.

bear.b: Substantial operating and free-cash-flow deficits show that the business currently consumes significant capital rather than funding itself internally. Continued losses could require additional external financing, reducing financial flexibility and potentially diluting existing shareholders.

The wide gap between early product sales and operating expenses demonstrates that commercial scale has not yet caught up with the cost structure. Until revenue grows materially or spending is reduced, the company is likely to remain dependent on its cash reserves and outside funding.

Weak retail uptake constrains distribution breadth and makes it harder to measure whether patient persistence extends beyond the e-pharmacy channel. Reliance on a narrower channel mix may limit prescription growth and leave commercial performance more dependent on targeted digital and telehealth efforts.
